description: 15:00 - Saw a goshawk fly over, heading south. 15:15 - Heard a goshawk alarm call, probably reacting to the gardeners driving by. Found droppings underneath old goshawk nest. 15:30 - Found pellet (https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/9575760), looks like pigeon remains. 16:00 (recording) - Waited near the goshawk's usual perching place (Tilia cordata). Male and female goshawks flew in. Female carrying prey. The female perched on a higher branch. The male beneath, hopping on a branch. It's rare to see male and female that close together, the size dimorphism is striking. The did not pay attention to me. Female flew away carrying prey, male followed. Chattering and single note calls as they flew in, while on the branch and as they flew off. Recorded with a directional microphone from 40m distance. 300 Hz low-cut filter. Normalized at -3dB. Urban setting, cemetery, street and work noises. Location obscured, due to poisoning incident in 2016. classificationBasis: 依据原作者逐文件物种、录音类型和备注，归为动物生物／鸟类；中文叫声或动作标签仅对应作者明确录音类型；未逐条听感审核。
description: Female adult goshawk. Perched on a lime tree (Tilia sp.). Same tree as [ XC395460 ] The goshawk saw me before I saw her, and called, reacting to my presence (alarm call). I then left the area. Recorded using a directional microphone, at ca. 35 m. Normalized to -3dB. 300Hz low cut filter. Urban setting, cemetery. Some microphone cable noise. I returned later that day before sunset. After making sure the goshawk was not there, I found rock pigeon feathers (Columbia livia) underneath the tree, in a pattern similar to [ XC396292 ], corresponding to prey butchered on a branch. At ca. 10m. distance from the tree, I found rests of a long-eared owl (Asio otus) butchered on the ground. I also found what I think is a pellet, so it appears the prey was eaten on the ground. I can rule out that the owl was the predator, as there were a lot of owl feathers and no feathers of any other bird. Thanks to Frank Holzapfel and Piotr Szczypinski for identifying the feathers (I first thought this was a kestrel). I collected feathers and posted a picture to iNaturalist ( https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/9241283 ). At around sunset (15:55), a goshawk called from another lime tree at ca. 90m. distance, and then flew into a spruce. description: Large goshawk, gray-brown wing covers, probably a female. Perched on a strikingly twisted branch of a black locust tree (Robinia pseudoacacia). Probably the branch is a good horizontal surface for eating. Observed for 16 minutes, from a distance of ca. 90 m. Obviously, the bird saw me, but did not pay attention to my presence. After having finished feeding, the bird moved around on the branches and called. After that, a second goshawk that had been hiding in a spruce (Picea abies) flew away to the other cemetery across the street. Recorded from ca. 90 m with a directional mic. Urban setting, traffic noises, cemetery. Sunset at 15:53. Normalized to -3dB. 300Hz low cut filter. Compare to the faster alarm call in [ XC395460 ]. (update 19.12.2017) I visited the area again on the next day. After making sure there were no goshawks around, I found pigeon feathers (Columba livia) on the ground around the goshawk's perch. I posted a picture of the feathers on iNaturalist for confirmation ( https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/9211076 ). description: A variety of calls from several birds foraging on the surface vegetation at the border of typha marsh and open water. The main vocalizer in this track was hidden in the cattails and not observed, though there were several other individuals visible and making similar calls. Observed from an observation deck at the end of a wooden walkway through the marsh. There were a large number of Soras in the immediate vicinity (they were moving through in large numbers on migration). 5-10 birds were almost always foraging in sight and many more hidden in the cattails, which resulted in quite a few squabbles between individuals. Unfortunately, a fair amount of traffic noise from a nearby highway, though some low-frequency noise was filtered out.
